ICT.question: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) refers to the technologies, including both hardware and software, that enable humans to communicate with one another.
The history of ICT is categorized into three main historical periods.
During the Premechanical Period, stone tablets were maintained as the final permanent storage medium because they were light and easy to carry.
The papyrus plant led to the first production of paper, which revolutionized how information was stored.
Libraries are considered the first data centers in human history.
The abacus was introduced by the Romans in the 2nd Century BCE but originated from China.
The Mechanical Period focused on machines that could enhance the speed and efficiency of calculations.
Charles Babbage is known as the Father of the Computers.
The Analytical Engine featured an arithmetic logic unit (ALU), integrated memory, and control flow.
The Electromechanical Period ushered in a new age by using electricity for long-distance communication.
The telegraph was invented in 1837 by William Cooke and Sir Charles Wheatstone.
Morse Code was invented by Samuel Morse in 1844 for use with the single-circuit telegraph.
Alexander Graham Bell was granted the patent for the telephone in 1876.
The Bombe was invented by Alan Turing in 1939 to decipher German encryption codes during World War II.
Gordon Welchman improved the Bombe in 1940.
The Electronic Period is focused on the advent of solid-state and electronic devices.
ENIAC stands for Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer.
ENIAC was a massive machine occupying 167 square meters.
The transistor was invented in 1947 as a faster, lightweight alternative to vacuum tubes.
An Integrated Circuit (IC) is a single package composed of a group of transistors and circuit elements.
The Olivetti Programma 101 was the first commercial personal computer sold in 1965.
The IBM 5150 was developed by a team led by Don Estridge.
The World Wide Web was proposed by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.
Web 1.0 is known as the read-and-write Web.
Web 2.0 allowed for interactivity, e-mail interaction, and social networking.
